highlights.title: SpaceX launches massive Starship rocket in first test flight since IPO
highlights.description: Elon Musk's rocket maker is conducting the first test fight for its massive Starship rocket since the company's IPO last month.

highlights.title: Samsung Inks $200 Billion Chip Supply with Broadcom
highlights.description: Samsung Electronics Co. won a contract worth more than $200 billion to make chips for Broadcom Inc., as the companies race to win a larger share of the AI infrastructure market.

highlights.title: SK Chair Says Anthropic Asked for Supplies to Make Its Own Chips
highlights.description: AI developer Anthropic PBC has asked SK Hynix Inc., one of the world’s biggest manufacturers of memory chips, for supplies to make its own semiconductors, SK Group Chairman Chey Tae Won said.

highlights.title: I tried out OpenAI’s new AI keypad — which will be fun for some coders and slightly mystifying to everyone else
highlights.description: OpenAI's fancy new AI keypad will be a lot of fun for some, while many others are probably not going to touch it.

highlights.title: New lawsuit alleges unpatchable Apple chip exploit was developed using stolen trade secrets
highlights.description: Magnet Forensics is suing Paradigm Shift Technology over its publication of usbliter8, alleging that the unpatchable exploit affecting several Apple SoCs was developed using trade secrets misappropriated by a former engineer. Here are the details.

highlights.title: SpaceX conducts 13th Starship test flight
highlights.description:
SpaceX launched Starship on its 13th suborbital test flight July 24, correcting some of the issues seen on the previous flight while deploying functioning satellites for the first time.
The post SpaceX conducts 13th Starship test flight appeared first on SpaceNews.

highlights.title: Report: Apple and Micron clash before Trump over Chinese memory chips
highlights.description: The Wall Street Journal reports that Micron is pressing the Trump administration to block Apple’s push to use memory chips from Chinese suppliers. Here are the details.

highlights.title: India’s Modi Adopts Reels Amid Instagram-Fueled Student Unrest
highlights.description: As student protests spread across India, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has turned to Meta Platforms Inc.’s Instagram Reels, swapping his trademark cinematic videos for raw, self-recorded messages aimed at the country’s youth.
